children: Marico, Tata Consumer and ITC are among Nomura's top picks in Consumer Staples, while Lenskart Solutions, Titan and United Spirits are its preferred names in Consumer Discretionary, as the brokerage remains watchful on rural demand amid a below-normal monsoon, El Niño and product price increases linked to the West Asia conflict.

In its India Consumer Global Markets Research note, Nomura said the southwest monsoon is around 15% below normal so far, versus the full-season forecast of 10% below normal, with a model error of -4%.

However, key kharif crop-growing regions have seen less deficit. Rainfall is 6% below normal in the Central region and 10% below normal in the Northwest region, compared with a 28% deficit in the South Peninsular region and 26% in the Eastern and North-eastern regions.

"The Central region is the most important region for kharif crop" as it has the highest saliency for key crops such as cotton, oilseeds, pulses, sugarcane, cereals and rice, Nomura said. Given the monsoon deficit in the region is only marginal versus the all-India deficit, "it could help cushion the overall impact on crop production and prices".

Kharif sowing was down 1.5% year-on-year as of September 11, improving from a 23% deficit as of June 25. Rice and maize sowing remained down 3.8% and 2.6%, respectively, while pulses improved 1.5% year-on-year.

Nomura said high buffer stocks should help keep inflation under check. As of August 16, government rice and wheat stocks were at 3x and 1.8x the buffer norm, respectively. The CCEA has also approved higher MSPs for 14 kharif crops for the 2026-27 marketing season and expects crop procurement of around 82.4 million tonnes.

However, reservoir levels remain a concern. Current live storage is around 7% below the past 10-year average, while storage in the Southern region has widened to around 25% below normal from 17% in August. "We remain watchful of its impact on kharif crops," Nomura said, adding that lower reservoir levels and below-normal rainfall could raise concerns about rabi sowing.

Nomura said it "remain[s] watchful on rural demand" as it faces multiple headwinds from the below-normal monsoon, El Niño and product price increases. While mid-single-digit overall inflation and price increases remain manageable, further price hikes and an impact on agricultural yields could add to pressure on demand and consumption.
The brokerage prefers companies with higher urban saliency, pricing power, strong brands, resilient portfolios and better execution.

title: Marico, Tata Consumer, ITC among Nomura top picks as monsoon deficit puts rural demand at risk
